question: What is the primary definition of the medicalisation of female genital mutilation?

options.A: The use of modern antibiotics to treat infections caused by traditional cutting
options.B: The surgical repair of female genitalia following traditional mutilation
options.C: The government funding of maternal health clinics in rural communities
options.D: The performance of FGM procedures by trained or untrained healthcare personnel

explanation: Medicalisation occurs when health workers perform any form of female genital mutilation, falsely implying that the procedure is safe. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why does the involvement of healthcare providers in performing FGM present a unique danger?

options.A: It universally causes immediate death from profound hemorrhage
options.B: It lends a false sense of clinical legitimacy to a harmful practice
options.C: It guarantees that no psychological trauma will occur later in life
options.D: It eliminates all risks of transmission of bloodborne pathogens

explanation: When doctors or nurses perform the procedure, communities may believe the act is medically sound and acceptable. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which sociocultural factor is most commonly cited by communities to justify female genital mutilation?

options.A: Ensuring premarital chastity and preserving family honor
options.B: Preventing chronic pelvic inflammatory disease in adolescents
options.C: Complying with modern international obstetric guidelines
options.D: Enhancing female fertility and boosting hormonal balance

explanation: Cultural beliefs heavily link the procedure to controlling female sexuality and maintaining social acceptance. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h2)

question: What motivates some healthcare workers to participate in medicalised FGM despite professional oaths?

options.A: Pressure from community traditions and financial incentives
options.B: Direct mandates from the World Health Organization
options.C: Strict legal protection granted by local medical councils
options.D: Scientific proof that cutting improves maternal outcomes

explanation: Internalized cultural norms and monetary rewards often drive health workers to compromise their ethical standards. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which complication is classified as an immediate physical risk of female genital mutilation?
explanation: The immediate trauma of cutting vascular genital tissue frequently triggers intense bleeding and extreme pain. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h3)

question: A primigravida client with a history of severe FGM is admitted in active labor. What outcome is she most likely to experience?

options.A: Obstructed labor due to rigid scar tissue obstructing the birth canal
options.B: Rapid, pain-free expulsion of the fetus through relaxed tissues
options.C: Spontaneous resolution of all previous psychological trauma
options.D: Complete absence of uterine contractions throughout the first stage

explanation: Fibrous scar tissue replaces pliable mucosal membranes, severely impeding normal fetal descent during childbirth. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which bioethical principle is fundamentally breached when a healthcare provider performs FGM on a minor?
explanation: Minors cannot grant informed consent, violating autonomy, while performing an unindicated surgery violates the core rule to do no harm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the legal consequence for a licensed nurse or doctor in Nigeria convicted of performing FGM?

options.A: A written warning placed in a confidential hospital file
options.B: Criminal prosecution, imprisonment, and loss of professional license
options.C: Mandatory reassignment to a rural administrative post
options.D: A mandatory three-day workshop on reproductive health ethics

explanation: Anti-FGM legislation and professional codes treat medicalisation as a serious criminal offense warranting jail time and license revocation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which international body joins the WHO in strictly condemning the medicalisation of FGM?
explanation: UNICEF works alongside the WHO and other global bodies to eliminate all forms of FGM, including medicalised procedures. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the official position of professional nursing regulatory councils regarding healthcare providers who perform FGM?

options.A: It is encouraged if performed under sterile operating room conditions
options.B: It is tolerated as a necessary cultural accommodation in rural zones
options.C: It is classified as professional misconduct subject to severe disciplinary action
options.D: It is permitted only if the patient signs a formal liability waiver

explanation: Regulatory bodies view cutting by clinicians as a grave breach of professional ethics and law. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h5)

question: When is a nurse most likely to identify a young girl at heightened risk for undergoing FGM?

options.A: During annual adult occupational health screenings
options.B: At the time of routine geriatric wellness evaluations
options.C: During routine pediatric visits prior to traditional holiday seasons

explanation: Families often schedule traditional rites or travel during school breaks and holiday periods, making proactive clinical screening vital. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h6)

question: A nurse overhears a colleague discussing plans to perform a 'minor, harmless nick' on a relative's newborn daughter. What immediate action should the nurse take?

options.A: Offer to assist the colleague to ensure sterile surgical technique is used
options.B: Ignore the conversation to maintain workplace harmony among staff
options.C: Intervene, educate the colleague on legal penalties, and report the ethical breach
options.D: Wait until the child turns eighteen before mentioning the incident

explanation: Nurses have a professional and legal obligation to prevent harm and report planned illegal acts of genital mutilation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which clinical approach is most essential when providing healthcare to a survivor of FGM?

options.C: Strict avoidance of any discussion regarding the genital area
options.D: Immediate surgical reversal without patient consent

explanation: Survivors require a safe, empathetic environment that respects their dignity and encourages open communication. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why is psychological support a critical component of nursing care for FGM survivors?

options.A: Psychological counseling replaces the need for any physical examination
options.B: The physical trauma is frequently compounded by deep emotional scars and PTSD
options.C: Emotional distress disappears spontaneously once adulthood is reached
options.D: Mental health interventions are mandated only for surgical complications

explanation: The procedure leaves lasting psychological impacts, including anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress, requiring dedicated mental health support. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h7)
